messages:
Maya: Quick posting — trying a compact priority scorecard for catalog onboards + a pin guardrail proposal. Want a short cycle of feedback before I formalize. TL;DR: three lanes, numeric triage score, fixed pin tiers, and automatic canary halts on concrete signals.

Jorge: Sounds useful. What are the lanes called?

Maya: Naming: Sprint (fast), Standard (default), Steward (lockdown). Sprint = fast onboarding for low-risk, public models. Standard = full harness + staged canary. Steward = private/VPC/regulatory or infra-heavy work; longer runway + legal/security checks.

Sophia: How do we compute the triage score?

Maya: Proposal (simple, auditable): score = round((impact_score * revenue_tier) / (infra_burden + eval_risk + kernel_flag)). impact_score 1-10, revenue_tier {community:1, paid:3, enterprise:5}, infra_burden 0.1-10, eval_risk 0-10, kernel_flag 0 or 1.5. Higher score = higher priority.

Max: Add clear infra multipliers so estimates are consistent: +50% infra_burden if new kernel; +25% if quant tuning; x3 if dedicated hardware requested.

Eva: Finance will want a worked example. Please include a row with a 10M token tenant and a 12% per-token cost delta so we can show $ impact and migration credit ballpark.

Maya: Will do. Canary defaults I propose: cohort = min(0.5% tenant traffic, 2k req/day), duration = 48h for chat/gen, 72h for embeddings. Auto-halt triggers: p50 latency > baseline +25ms OR error rate increase >4% OR eval safety drop >2.5pts OR hallucination_rate >1.4x baseline.

Sophia: Add a semantic anchor set (5–10 prompts) per-tenant that runs during canary and post-rollout to detect customer-specific regressions.

Maya: Agreed. Also propose pin TTL tiers: 14d / 60d / 365d. Pins >60d require either reserved capacity or paid migration credits. Pin-exemptions (longer holds) allowed but must include legal + security signoff and a backport SLA.

Jorge: For Private deployments where customers insist on long pins, are we offering a timeline for backports/security patches?

Maya: Exemption request must include an agreed patch SLA (e.g., critical fixes within 30 days) and a scoping of who pays for emergency backports. Keep exemptions rare and logged.

Max: Who runs the end-to-end harness and the canary flip? Platform does orchestration and automated triggers; model owner provides eval artifacts, anchor prompts, and signs off on each rollout step.

Sophia: Can we gate rollout steps on automated eval checks? If the harness flags regression at any step, pipeline halts and notifies owners.

Maya: Yes — harness gates are required for Standard and Steward lanes. Sprint may waive some checks if infra_burden and eval_risk are low.

rollout-bot: Canary launched for "demo-model-z" on tenant "BetaCorp" — cohort=640 req/day, duration=48h. Monitoring hooks enabled.

Eva: +1 but reiterating billing example demand. Also include a short table of common infra multipliers in the RFC.

Maya: Noted. I'll draft a compact RFC + scoring spreadsheet and publish tomorrow with two billing worked examples and three infra multiplier scenarios. Scheduling a 30–45m slot to finalize thresholds. Please react here with quick thumbs.
